title: Stakeholder
description: A motivation element naming a person, group, team, organization, or class of such parties, by its role or perspective, whose interests or concerns about the architecture are what drivers, goals, and requirements are traced back to. It captures who cares and why, not who performs behavior. Use Driver instead when the element states the concern or condition itself (e.g. 'GDPR fines', 'customer churn') rather than the party who holds it. Use Requirement instead when the text is a need the system must satisfy, such as a user story 'As a clerk I want…', where the clerk is only the associated stakeholder. Use Value instead when the element expresses the worth or benefit a party gains, rather than the party itself.

documentation.description: Free-text description of the stakeholder's role, scope, and principal concerns or interests in the architecture. Set it whenever the name alone does not make clear who the party is or what it cares about.

type.description: Classification of the stakeholder's relationship to the organization

x-dr-evidence: A 'Stakeholders' section or RACI table in a README, architecture document, or ADR that lists named roles or teams together with their concerns
MADR or ADR front-matter fields such as 'deciders', 'consulted', or 'informed' that list teams, roles, or external bodies
Compliance or requirements documents that name an external authority or audience (e.g. 'PCI SSC', 'data protection officer', 'merchant partners') as the source of an obligation or concern
